content:
Today, Instapaper released version 10 of its iPhone and iPad apps, featuring a number of improvements, along with a major redesign of the web platform. Details below.

"The biggest update to the iOS app in more than a decade"

Instapaper announced today (via MacMagazine) updates to its iOS apps, along with the introduction of new AI voice features for the Android app and a comprehensive website overhaul.

Instapaper version 10 for iOS adds support for Liquid Glass and introduces four reading fonts:

Literata: A serif font designed by Google for Google Play Books. New York: A serif font designed by Apple for iOS. Open Sans: A sans-serif font commissioned by Google. Atkinson Hyperlegible: A sans-serif font developed by the Braille Institute.

This update also adds a Home Screen widget, which Instapaper says can display the article you're currently reading and your most recently saved items, allowing you to start reading with a single tap.

Instapaper says the update improves multitasking for iPad users, while both iPhone and iPad users will notice more reliable background syncing, faster article download times, and a redesigned onboarding tour.

Instapaper says this is the biggest update in over a decade, and includes the following:

Section Counts: All sections will now display the number of articles or notes they contain. If you find section counts more anxiety-inducing than helpful, you can disable them under Settings > Behavior > Section Counts. Section Sorting: To sort your folders or labels, tap the "…" menu next to a section header and choose your preferred sort order. Article List Appearance: We've added Condensed View, new font typography and styles, and a simple way to customize the appearance of article lists. In an article list, tap "…", then tap "Appearance" to adjust style, fonts, and image thumbnails.

Finally, Instapaper has comprehensively updated its web platform, adding features including a three-pane reader and keyboard shortcuts, while the Android app now also supports AI voice.
